subject: MSA/Order Form: Harmonize renewal windows and TFC playbook for pilot -> prod
messages:
From: Procurement ACME <procurement@acme.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Olson <dana.olson@acmelegal.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on renewal term & TFC carveout in latest MSA

Hi Camila,

Thanks for sending the MSA and order form last week. Our legal team has two quick asks before we move to signatures:

1) Auto-renew: the MSA currently auto-renews for one-year terms unless either party provides 60 days' written notice. Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a 90-day opt-out for enterprise pilots that convert to paid production; our procurement prefers longer notice windows for budgeting.

2) Termination for Convenience (TFC): we need to understand the proposed cap on termination liability during a pilot-to-production migration. Specifically, would Redwood agree to a 30-day transition support commitment post-TFC and a mutual limitation on exit assistance fees?

We'd appreciate a redline indicating your compromise positions so our counsel can wrap this up.

Best,
Marco Ruiz
Head of Procurement, ACME Corporation
procurement@acme.com

Attachment: acme_redlines_mark1.pdf (pdf)
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Marco Ruiz <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Dana Olson <dana.olson@acmelegal.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on renewal term & TFC carveout in latest MSA

Marco — thanks for the clear asks. Quick response while I loop in Legal:

- Auto-renew: We can move to a 90-day opt-out for pilot accounts that convert to enterprise paid plans, but we'd want to preserve standard 60-day notice for typical order forms.
- TFC: We're open to a fixed 30-day transition support period post-TFC for pilot-conversion customers, with a capped support fee equal to the prorated monthly charges for those 30 days (to cover orderly handoff).

Putting Karthik on copy for legal redline language. I'll follow up with a redline and an order-form amendment that explicitly tags pilot accounts so the 90-day opt-out only applies to those pilots.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Camila.Reyes@redwood.com
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: none
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on renewal term & TFC carveout in latest MSA

Camila — drafting notes below for the redline. I'll attach the docx with tracked changes. High level: preserve our standard cadence but carve a bounded exception for pilots converting to production. Proposed language fragments:

- Auto-Renewal (Order Form): For Pilot Accounts (defined in Order Form as an account with initial committed term < 6 months or designated "pilot" at time of purchase), notice to non-renew shall be 90 days. For all other Order Forms, notice to non-renew remains 60 days.

- Termination for Convenience (MSA): Either party may terminate for convenience with 30 days' notice; for Pilot Accounts that transition to paid usage, Redwood will provide transition support not to exceed 30 calendar days and will invoice a transition-support fee not to exceed the prorated monthly charges for the account for the remainder of the then-current billing month.

- Liability & Exit Assistance: Limit exit assistance obligations to operational handoff and reasonable cooperation; no extended runbook or custom engineering expected under TFC unless separately contracted.

Questions for Commercial: are we comfortable with the fee cap being prorated monthly charges (vs. a flat fixed-dollar cap)? That limits exposure but remains simple for ACME to compute.

Attaching: redlined_msa_v2.docx

-Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on renewal term & TFC carveout in latest MSA

Thanks Karthik — Laura, fyi on negotiation posture. A couple of commercial notes from my side:

- ACME asks for 90 days on all renewals; we should limit 90-day to pilots only.
- On the fee cap: LAURA recommends a hard cap for predictability (e.g., no more than $15k) because ACME has large volume and prorated calculation could balloon if usage spikes. Thoughts?

If legal prefers prorated approach, I can push back and offer a blended compromise: prorated monthly charges capped at $15k. That gives us both exposure control and a logical formula.

Can you put that blended language in the redline? If so I can push this final to Marco + Dana tonight.

-Camila
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on renewal term & TFC carveout in latest MSA

Camila/Laura — agreed, blended language makes sense. Updated redline attached and I added a short playbook note in a text file describing what "transition support" covers (LDAP transfer, KV cache dump, three (3) hours of ops consult, no custom feature work).

Proposed final snippet to send to ACME: 

"For Pilot Accounts, the non-renewal notice period shall be 90 days. For all other accounts, non-renewal notice shall be 60 days. In the event of termination for convenience with respect to a Pilot Account, Redwood will provide up to thirty (30) calendar days of transition support. Redwood's transition-support fee will be the prorated monthly charges for the account for those thirty (30) days, provided that such fee shall not exceed Fifteen Thousand Dollars (US $15,000). Transition support includes operational handover activities limited to (i) account configuration export, (ii) assistance with DNS and endpoint cutover, and (iii) up to three (3) hours of remote operations consultation. Any additional professional services will be quoted and invoiced separately."

If that language is acceptable, I'll attach redlined_msa_v2.docx and orderform_amendment.pdf and send to ACME with a DocuSign link.

-Karthik
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Marco Ruiz <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Dana Olson <dana.olson@acmelegal.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Final MSA/Order Form compromise and next steps (DocuSign link)

Marco / Dana — thanks for the patience while we hashed this out. Attached are: (1) redlined_msa_v2.docx with the blended language, (2) orderform_amendment.pdf tagging the pilot account, and (3) TFC_playbook_notes.txt summarizing what transition support includes.

Summary of the compromise:
- Pilot accounts: 90-day non-renewal notice.
- Standard accounts: 60-day non-renewal notice (no change).
- TFC for Pilot accounts: 30-day transition support; fee = prorated monthly charges for those 30 days, capped at US $15,000. Playbook limits are included in the text file.

If this matches ACME's expectations, please sign the amendment via DocuSign here: https://docusign.com/sandbox/ABC123-def. We can expedite countersignature and flip to production once signed.

Attachments: redlined_msa_v2.docx (docx), orderform_amendment.pdf (pdf), TFC_playbook_notes.txt (txt)

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
